People confuse consensus with buy-in, and the confusion is expensive. Silence in a meeting almost never means agreement. It usually means somebody has decided that the conversation is not worth having in public, which is a very different thing. My test for real buy-in is simple, and it has nothing to do with what happens in the room. Would this person defend the idea in a room you are not in? If the answer is no, you do not have buy-in. You have politeness. The other thing I would tell anyone in your position is to name the trade-off yourself. Every proposal costs somebody something. If you name that cost, it reads as judgement and people trust the rest of what you say. If they find it, it becomes a weakness in your case and you spend the meeting defending instead of deciding. People who only present get surprised twice. Once when the proposal is approved, and again six months later when nothing at all has happened.

When I moved into a group where everything happened in English, my presentations were fine and my influence collapsed. It took me a year to understand why. Influence does not live in presentations. It lives in the unscripted conversations, and those were exactly the ones I was avoiding. A presentation you can prepare. A corridor has no agenda, no slides and no second draft, so everything that makes a presentation feel safe is missing. What I started doing sounds ridiculous and it worked. I prepared the informal conversations the way I prepared the formal ones. Three sentences, written on paper, before I picked up the phone. What I want, what it costs them, and what I am asking for specifically. The calls came out slightly stiff for the first month, and here is the part that surprised me: nobody minded. The awkwardness was entirely mine. It went away, and the influence came back.

Before I put this on an agenda, where would you land on it? I know what this costs your market. Let me tell you what it buys it. If this comes up when I am not in the room, would you be willing to get behind it? Two markets are already behind it, and what I need from you is the decision itself.
